tool:EditPhoto.summary: Adjusts the light, colour, detail and effects of a photo with sliders and a live preview, then saves an edited copy.
tool:EditPhoto.details: Edit Photo opens the photo with a live preview, a colour histogram and nineteen sliders in four groups: Light (Exposure, Brightness, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Gamma), Color (Temperature, Tint, Saturation, Vibrance, Hue), Detail (Clarity, Sharpness, Noise Reduction) and Effects (Dehaze, Grain, Vignette). Every slider starts at 0; double-click a slider or press its small reset arrow to put it back, and Reset puts them all back. Hold the Hold to compare button, or the backslash key, to see the original while you work. Save Edited Copy applies the same changes to the full-size photo and saves it next to the original as 'name Edited' in the same format, keeping its details and colour profile.
tool:EditPhoto.how: Drag one photo, tap Ctrl and drop on EDIT; move the sliders and choose Save Edited Copy.
examples: A dark birthday photo taken indoors: raise Exposure and Shadows until faces are clear.
A beach picture that looks washed out: add Dehaze and a little Vibrance before posting it on Instagram.
An old scanned print with a yellow cast: move Temperature towards blue and add Noise Reduction.
tool:EditPhoto.worksOn: One picture at a time (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, TIFF, AVIF, BMP and similar).

tool:AnnotatePhoto.summary: Draws arrows, text, boxes, highlights and numbered steps on a picture and saves an annotated PNG copy.
tool:AnnotatePhoto.details: Annotate Photo shows the picture with a strip of nine tools: Arrow, Highlighter, Text, Rectangle, Ellipse, Draw, Numbered step, Magnifier and Insert image (which places another picture on top). Pick a colour with the colour well; drag an annotation to move it, double-click text to edit it, and use Undo (Ctrl+Z) or Delete selected (Del) to fix mistakes. Reset clears everything you added. Save Annotated Copy saves the result next to the original as 'name Annotated.png', always as PNG.
tool:AnnotatePhoto.how: Drag one picture, tap Ctrl and drop on ANNOTATE; pick a tool, draw on the picture and choose Save Annotated Copy.
examples: A screenshot of a settings page for a colleague: add an arrow and the text 'click here'.
A setup guide for a parent: mark three buttons with Numbered step 1, 2 and 3.
A photo of a car scratch for the insurance: circle it with Ellipse and enlarge it with Magnifier.

tool:AddBackground.summary: Places a picture on a gradient, colour or image background with padding, rounded corners and a shadow.
tool:AddBackground.details: Add Background puts the picture on a background with a live preview. Choose one of twelve soft gradients (Dawn, Lagoon, Aurora, Peach, Ultraviolet, Mint, Sky, Ember, Night, Blush, Citrus, Graphite), one of eighteen solid colours, your own colour, or an image of your own, which also gets a Blur slider. Padding, Corners and Shadow start at sizes that suit the picture, and Ratio can be Auto, 1:1, 16:9, 4:5 or 9:16. Save with Background saves the result next to the original as 'name Background' in the same format; Reset goes back to the defaults.
tool:AddBackground.how: Drag one picture, tap Ctrl and drop on ADD BG; pick a background, set Padding, Corners and Shadow, then choose Save with Background.
examples: A plain app screenshot for a LinkedIn post: put it on the Aurora gradient with rounded corners and a shadow.
A product photo for an Instagram story: choose Ratio 9:16 and a solid colour behind it.
A code snippet image for a slide: give it white padding at 16:9 so it fits the slide.

tool:CropImage.summary: Cuts a picture down to the part you want, freely or to a ratio or exact size, for one picture or many.
tool:CropImage.details: With one picture, Crop Image shows it with a crop box you drag; Aspect ratio can be Free, 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3 or 3:4, and you can type the size in pixels in the W and H boxes. With several pictures, each one is cropped around its centre to the ratio you choose (1:1 at first), or to an Exact size, where each picture is scaled to cover that size and then trimmed; leave the size empty to keep each picture's own resolution. Apply saves each result next to its original as 'name Cropped' in the same format. Reset (one picture) puts the crop box back.
tool:CropImage.how: Drag one or more pictures, tap Ctrl and drop on CROP; set the box or the ratio and choose Apply.
examples: A group photo where you only want your friend: drag the box around them and choose Apply.
Twenty product photos for an online shop that need to be square: drop them all and choose 1:1.
A banner for a website that must be exactly 1200 by 630 pixels: type W 1200 and H 630.
tool:CropImage.worksOn: Pictures; one to crop by hand, or many cropped the same way. Also the pictures in a dropped folder.

tool:RedactPhoto.summary: Covers private details, faces or text in a picture with solid boxes or a blur that can't be undone.
tool:RedactPhoto.details: When Redact Photo opens it already looks for private details (e-mail addresses, phone numbers, card numbers, IBANs, IP addresses and passwords) and covers them; the Faces and Text buttons find faces and lines of text the same way, all on this PC with Windows' own detection. You can also drag on the photo to cover any area, drag a box to move it, drag its corner to resize it, and press Delete to remove it. Style is Solid (black at first, any colour you pick) or Blur, which is made so it can't be reversed. Save Redacted Copy saves the result next to the original as 'name Redacted'; the original stays as it is.
tool:RedactPhoto.how: Drag one picture, tap Ctrl and drop on REDACT; check the boxes, add your own and choose Save Redacted Copy. PRIVATE SHOT on the Screen wheel opens it on a fresh screenshot.
examples: A screenshot of a bank transfer to share in a group chat: the card number and IBAN are covered as the window opens.
A photo from a school trip for a public post: press Faces to blur the other children.
A picture of a parcel label for a seller: drag a box over your home address.

tool:ResizeImage.summary: Makes pictures larger or smaller, turns them a quarter turn and flips them, one picture or a whole selection.
tool:ResizeImage.details: Resize & Rotate offers Keep, Percent (50% at first, from 5% to 200%), Width, Height or Fit, which keeps the picture within a width and height you type; proportions are always kept. Allow making images larger lets Width, Height and Fit go above the original size, and when a picture comes out larger, Enlarge with AI for sharper detail uses the Real-ESRGAN model that ships with DropWheel (pictures up to about 4 megapixels). Rotate left, Rotate right, Flip horizontally and Flip vertically are under Turn; one picture shows a live preview with the size before and after. Save writes each result next to its original as 'name Resized' in the same format.
tool:ResizeImage.how: Drag one or more pictures, tap Ctrl and drop on RESIZE; pick a size and any turn, then choose Save.
examples: A 6000-pixel camera photo too big for a website upload: choose Width 1600.
A small 400-pixel logo needed for a poster: choose Percent 200 and leave AI enlargement on.
Holiday photos that came out sideways: drop them all and press Rotate right.
tool:ResizeImage.worksOn: Pictures; one with a live preview or many with the same settings. Also the pictures in a dropped folder.

tool:Watermark.summary: Puts your text or logo on pictures, on every frame of a video, or on every page of a PDF.
tool:Watermark.details: Add Watermark has two kinds: Text (Arabic included; '© year' at first) with a Colour (white at first), or Picture, a logo you choose. Size goes from 5% to 90% (30% at first) and Opacity from 10% to 100% (60% at first). Position is one of nine spots (bottom right at first), or tick Repeat across to cover the whole picture. A preview shows the first file, and DropWheel remembers your last watermark for next time. Each result is saved next to its original as 'name Watermarked'.
tool:Watermark.how: Drag files, tap Ctrl and drop on WATERMARK; set the text or picture, size and position, then choose Add Watermark.
examples: Thirty wedding photos for a client preview: drop them all and add your studio name in the bottom right corner.
A price list PDF you send to customers: add 'Confidential' with Repeat across on every page.
A cooking video for TikTok: put your logo picture in the top left corner of every frame.
tool:Watermark.worksOn: Pictures, videos (not GIFs) and PDFs; one file or many. Also the files in a dropped folder.

tool:CopyText.summary: Copies the text in a picture, or what a QR code or barcode in it says, to the clipboard at once.
tool:CopyText.details: Copy Text or QR Code needs no window. It first looks for QR codes and barcodes and copies what they say; when the code holds a web link, a click on the card opens it. With no code, it reads the picture's text with Windows' own text recognition, trying every language installed in Windows and keeping the cleanest reading, so Arabic and English both work. A card shows how many lines were copied and the first words. If nothing is found, it suggests a sharper picture or adding the language under Windows Settings › Time & language.
tool:CopyText.how: Drag one picture, tap Ctrl and drop on TEXT · QR; the text is on the clipboard, ready to paste with Ctrl+V.
examples: A screenshot of an error message: drop it and paste the text into a search or an e-mail.
A photo of a Wi-Fi QR code on a café table: the code's contents are copied straight away.
A photo of a printed Arabic recipe: drop it and paste the words into a note.
tool:CopyText.worksOn: One picture (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, TIFF, AVIF, BMP and similar).

tool:RemoveBackground.summary: Cuts the subject out of a photo, hair included, onto a transparent, white or coloured background.
tool:RemoveBackground.details: Remove Background uses the BiRefNet lite AI model on this PC; the 224 MB model downloads once from the tool's window the first time. Background can be Transparent (the default), White or Colour, and Crop to the subject trims the empty edges. A transparent result is saved as PNG unless the original is already PNG or WebP; each result goes next to its original as 'name No Background'. It runs on the processor, so older computers can take up to half a minute per picture. Resting on the petal before you drop shows the cut-out in the centre of the wheel once the model is there.
tool:RemoveBackground.how: Drag one or more pictures, tap Ctrl and drop on REMOVE BG; choose the background and press Remove Background.
examples: A product photo for an online shop: choose White for a clean listing picture.
A portrait for a sticker or a slide: keep Transparent and tick Crop to the subject.
Fifteen staff photos for a website: drop them all and give each the same blue background.
tool:RemoveBackground.worksOn: Pictures; one or many at once. Also the pictures in a dropped folder.

tool:EraseObject.summary: Removes unwanted things from a photo: brush over them and AI fills the area in.
tool:EraseObject.details: Erase Object uses the LaMa AI model on this PC; the 208 MB model downloads once from the tool's window. Brush over what should go (Brush size from 6 to 80 pixels, 22 at first), a little beyond its edges, then press Erase. You can brush and erase again as often as you like, and Undo steps back up to six times. Save Copy saves the result next to the original as 'name Erased'.
tool:EraseObject.how: Drag one photo, tap Ctrl and drop on ERASE; brush over the object, press Erase, then Save Copy.
examples: A holiday photo with a stranger walking behind you: brush over them and press Erase.
A house photo for a rental listing with a rubbish bin in front: erase the bin.
A sunset picture crossed by a power line: brush along the cable and erase it.

tool:ExportLayers.summary: Saves every layer of a Photoshop file as its own PNG, named after the layer, without Photoshop.
tool:ExportLayers.details: Export Layers reads PSD and PSB files and shows how many layers there are and how many are hidden. Each layer can be saved Cropped to the layer (the default) or On the full canvas, in its place on a transparent picture the size of the document. Include hidden layers adds the layers that are switched off. The PNGs are named after the layers and numbered from the top of the Layers panel, for example '03 Header - Logo.png', in a folder beside the file called 'name Layers'.
tool:ExportLayers.how: Drag one or more PSD files, tap Ctrl and drop on LAYERS; choose how each layer is saved and press Export Layers.
examples: A designer's website mockup PSD: get every icon and button as separate PNGs for the developer.
A poster with text layers switched off: tick Include hidden layers to get them too.
Character layers for an animation: choose On the full canvas so every PNG lines up.
tool:ExportLayers.worksOn: Photoshop files (PSD, PSB); one or many. Also the PSD files in a dropped folder.

tool:SlimPhotoshop.summary: Makes Photoshop files smaller by removing the hidden list of every file ever pasted in, leaving layers untouched.
tool:SlimPhotoshop.details: Remove Photoshop History runs straight away, with no window. Photoshop keeps adding a hidden list of every file ever pasted or placed into a document (its document ancestors), which can make a PSD many times larger than its pictures. DropWheel saves a copy without that list next to the original as 'name Slim'; layers and pixels are not changed. The card says how much smaller the files became.
tool:SlimPhotoshop.how: Drag one or more PSD files, tap Ctrl and drop on HISTORY; the slim copies appear next to them.
examples: A 900 MB PSD that should be about 80 MB: drop it on HISTORY and compare the sizes.
A design file too big to e-mail to a printer: slim it first, then send the copy.
A project folder of PSDs filling your cloud storage: drop the folder and slim them all.
tool:SlimPhotoshop.worksOn: Photoshop files (PSD, PSB); one or many. Also the PSD files in a dropped folder.

tool:SavePreview.summary: Saves the preview picture stored inside an EPS, InDesign or XD file as a PNG, without Adobe apps.
tool:SavePreview.details: Save Preview runs straight away, with no window. It takes the picture these files keep for previews and saves it next to the file as 'name Preview.png'. EPS needs no extra program for this. If a file holds no preview picture, the card says 'This file has no preview picture.'
tool:SavePreview.how: Drag the file, tap Ctrl and drop on PREVIEW; the PNG appears next to it.
examples: An InDesign brochure a client sent when you don't have InDesign: see what it looks like as a PNG.
An old EPS logo from a supplier: save its preview to drop into a presentation.
Ten XD design files to show in a meeting: drop them all and get a picture of each.
tool:SavePreview.worksOn: One EPS file, or one or more InDesign (INDD, INDT) or Adobe XD files.

tool:Palette.summary: Shows the colours of an ASE or ACO swatch file, copies them and saves them as CSS, JSON, GIMP or a picture.
tool:Palette.details: Colour Palette opens a swatch file from Photoshop, Illustrator or InDesign and shows each colour with its name and hex value. Click a colour to copy its hex value, or Copy All to copy every name and value. Save as offers CSS (the default), JSON, GIMP and Picture (a PNG sheet of the colours); the file is saved next to the swatch file with the same name and the new extension.
tool:Palette.how: Drag one ASE or ACO file, tap Ctrl and drop on PALETTE; click colours to copy them or choose a format and press Save.
examples: A brand colours ASE file from the design team: save it as CSS for the website.
A colour scheme you want to show in an e-mail: save it as Picture.
A Photoshop ACO palette you want in GIMP: save it as GIMP.

tool:ExtractColours.summary: Finds the main colours of a picture and saves them as swatches for Photoshop, Illustrator, code or a picture.
tool:ExtractColours.details: Extract Colours shows the picture and its main colours, 6 at first; the Colours slider picks from 3 to 12. Click a colour to copy its hex value. Save as offers ASE (the default; it opens in Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign through Swatches panel › Import), ACO (Photoshop's own), CSS and Picture. Save Colours saves the file next to the picture as 'name Colours' with that extension.
tool:ExtractColours.how: Drag one picture, tap Ctrl and drop on COLOURS; choose how many colours and a format, then press Save Colours.
examples: A sunset photo you want to use as a website theme: save 5 colours as CSS.
A client's logo before designing a flyer: save the colours as ASE and import them into Illustrator.
A painting for a bedroom makeover: click each colour to copy its code for the paint shop.
tool:ExtractColours.worksOn: One picture: JPG, PNG and the like, a Photoshop file, a camera RAW photo, an Illustrator file or an SVG.

tool:CreateCollage.summary: Puts several pictures together into one collage picture in a grid, row, column or featured layout.
tool:CreateCollage.details: Create Collage shows a live preview. Style is Grid (with Columns from 1 to 6), Row, Column or Featured, with one large picture on the left and the rest stacked on the right. Canvas can be Square 1:1 (the default), Portrait 4:5, Story 9:16, Landscape 16:9 or Photo 3:2, and Width 1,080, 2,048 (the default), 3,000 or 4,096 px. Image fit fills the cells by cropping the edges, or fits whole images. Under Spacing & background you set Spacing (24 px), Corners (16 px) and the Background colour (white), and under Image order you change the order. Create Collage saves a PNG named after the first picture, 'name Collage.png'.
tool:CreateCollage.how: Drag two or more pictures, tap Ctrl and drop on COLLAGE; pick a style and canvas, then press Create Collage.
examples: Four photos from a weekend away for an Instagram post: Grid with 2 columns on a square canvas.
A before and after of a kitchen renovation: Row with two pictures side by side.
Six product shots for a story: Featured on Story 9:16 with the best one large.
tool:CreateCollage.worksOn: Two or more pictures at once, Photoshop, RAW, SVG, Illustrator and EPS files included.

tool:DescribePicture.summary: Writes what a picture shows, as one sentence of alt text or a paragraph, with a small AI model on this PC.
tool:DescribePicture.details: Describe Picture uses the SmolVLM picture model on this PC; the first time, the model downloads once from the window (about 570 MB with the program that runs it). Length is A sentence (the default) or A paragraph. The words appear in a box you can change; in a language other than English they are translated on this PC, after a one-time translation model download. Copy puts the text on the clipboard, and Save in the Picture writes it into the picture's own details for JPG, PNG and WebP files without changing the picture. Check the words before you publish them.
tool:DescribePicture.how: Drag one picture, tap Ctrl and drop on DESCRIBE; wait for the words, edit them if needed and press Copy.
examples: A product photo for a website: copy the sentence as the picture's alt text.
A photo for a Facebook post read by a blind friend's screen reader: write a paragraph describing it.
A scanned family photo you want to find again later: use Save in the Picture so the description stays inside the file.
tool:DescribePicture.worksOn: One picture at a time; Save in the Picture works for JPG, PNG and WebP.

tool:TableFromImage.summary: Reads a table in a picture or screenshot into an Excel sheet, with rows, columns and real numbers.
tool:TableFromImage.details: Table to Excel runs straight away, with no window. It reads the picture with the text recognition built into Windows: words close together become a cell, and cells that line up become a column. Numbers are saved as numbers, Arabic tables keep their right-to-left order, and empty cells are read a second time on their own. Each sheet is saved next to its picture as 'name Table.xlsx'. If there is no table, the card says 'No table was found in this picture.'
tool:TableFromImage.how: Drag one or more pictures, tap Ctrl and drop on TABLE; the Excel file appears next to each picture.
examples: A screenshot of a sales report someone sent in a chat: get it as a sheet you can add up.
A photo of a printed price list from a supplier: turn it into Excel to compare prices.
Ten pictures of timetable pages: drop them all and get one Excel file for each.
tool:TableFromImage.worksOn: Pictures; one or many at once. Also the pictures in a dropped folder.

tool:Metadata.summary: Shows, edits and removes the hidden details in files, like where and when a photo was taken and the camera.
tool:Metadata.details: With one file, Metadata shows a summary (Camera, Taken, Location, Author) and every field grouped as Image, Camera (EXIF), Location (GPS), XMP, Movie, PDF and File, with a search box. Fields that can be changed are text boxes, and the minus button removes a field; Save writes your changes to a copy named 'name Edited'. Remove All strips location, camera, author and editing history and saves a clean copy named 'name No Metadata'; for photos it also clears hidden camera data but keeps colour and orientation. With several files, Remove All is the one action and cleans them all; the originals always stay as they are.
tool:Metadata.how: Drag files, tap Ctrl and drop on METADATA; edit or remove fields and press Save, or press Remove All.
examples: A photo of your new flat before posting it online: Remove All so nobody sees where it was taken.
A PDF report with the wrong author name: change the Author field and press Save.
Fifty phone videos for a public YouTube channel: drop them all and press Remove All.
tool:Metadata.worksOn: Pictures, videos, GIFs, audio files and PDFs; one file to see and edit every field, or many to clean at once. Also the files in a dropped folder.

tool:NormalizeAudio.summary: Makes a recording's volume even and as loud as you choose, so quiet and loud files end up matching.
tool:NormalizeAudio.details: Normalize Volume measures how loud a recording is and brings it to a target level in two passes, using the EBU R128 loudness standard. For one file the window shows the waveform, a Play button and the level it has now (LUFS, peak and range). You set Target loudness (-24 to -5 LUFS, default -16), Loudness range (1 to 20 LU, default 11) and True peak limit (-9 to 0 dBTP, default -1.5), which helps prevent clipping; Reset puts the defaults back. The result keeps the original format and is saved beside it as 'name Normalized'. A completely silent file can't be normalized.
tool:NormalizeAudio.how: Drag one or more audio files, tap Ctrl and drop on NORMALIZE; change the sliders if you want and choose Normalize Audio.
examples: Six podcast episodes recorded at different levels: drop them all and each is saved as 'episode Normalized.mp3' at the same loudness.
A voice memo too quiet to hear in the car: the default -16 LUFS makes it clearly audible.
A party playlist where some songs blast and others whisper: normalize them so nobody reaches for the volume knob.
tool:NormalizeAudio.worksOn: Audio files (MP3, M4A, WAV, FLAC, OGG, OPUS, AIFF, WMA); one or many at once.

tool:TrimAudio.summary: Cuts the start and end off a recording, keeping just the part you choose.
tool:TrimAudio.details: Trim Audio shows the recording's waveform with two handles: drag the ends to choose the part to keep, or type exact times in the Start and End boxes. The header shows how long the selection is, and Play Selected Range lets you listen before saving. Trim silent ends automatically moves the handles to where the sound really starts and stops; silence in the middle is kept. Choose Apply to save the kept part beside the original as 'name Trimmed', in the same format.
tool:TrimAudio.how: Drag one audio file, tap Ctrl and drop on TRIM; drag the ends of the waveform and choose Apply.
examples: A 40-minute lecture recording with 5 minutes of chatter before it starts: drag the start handle past the chatter.
A ringtone from the chorus of a song: type Start 0:45 and End 1:15 and choose Apply.
A voice note with long silence at both ends: tick Trim silent ends automatically.

tool:AudioChannels.summary: Turns a recording into mono or stereo and sets the volume of the left and right sides separately.
tool:AudioChannels.details: Convert Audio Channels shows the left (L) and right (R) channels as waveforms, each with a play button to hear it alone. Output is Mono or Stereo (default Stereo), and Left volume and Right volume go from 0 to 200% (default 100%). Play Output lets you hear the result before saving. A mono recording becomes two identical channels in stereo, and a file with more than two channels is folded down to stereo first. Choose Apply; the result is saved as 'name Stereo' or 'name Mono' in the same format.
tool:AudioChannels.how: Drag one audio file, tap Ctrl and drop on CHANNELS; pick Mono or Stereo, set the volumes and choose Apply.
examples: An interview where the guest is only in the left ear: choose Mono so both ears hear both voices.
A recording where the right side is much louder: lower Right volume to 60%.
A mono voice-over that a video editor asked for in stereo: choose Stereo.

tool:AudioVisualizer.summary: Turns a song or recording into an MP4 video with moving waveform bars or a still picture.
tool:AudioVisualizer.details: Audio Visualizer makes a video out of sound, for places that only take videos. Style is Waveform (animated bars in the colour you pick, on black) or Still image (a picture you choose with Choose image… fills the frame; PNG, JPG, WEBP or BMP). Shape is 16:9 (1920 × 1080), 9:16 (1080 × 1920) or 1:1 (1080 × 1080), and the preview shows the shape and colour. Choose Create Visualization: the result is an MP4 (H.264 with AAC sound) at 30 frames a second, as long as the audio, saved as 'name Visualizer.mp4'.
tool:AudioVisualizer.how: Drag one audio file, tap Ctrl and drop on VISUALIZE; choose a style, shape and colour, then Create Visualization.
examples: A podcast clip for Instagram Reels: Waveform, 9:16, in your brand colour.
A song for YouTube with its album cover: Still image, 16:9.
A voice message to post where only videos are allowed: Waveform, 1:1 square.

tool:BleepAudio.summary: Covers chosen moments of a recording with a bleep tone, for swear words or private details.
tool:BleepAudio.details: Bleep Audio shows the recording's waveform under a Bleep layer. Drag across the Bleep layer to add a section, drag a clip or either edge to adjust it, and press Delete to remove the selected one; the number of bleeps is shown at the top. Under Preview, Original and With Bleeps let you listen before saving. Choose Save Bleeped Copy: each section is replaced by a 1 kHz tone and the copy is saved as 'name Bleeped' in the same format. You need at least one section.
tool:BleepAudio.how: Drag one audio file, tap Ctrl and drop on BLEEP; drag across the Bleep layer over each word, then choose Save Bleeped Copy.
examples: A podcast where a guest swears twice: add two bleeps over the words before publishing.
A recorded call where someone reads out a card number: bleep it before sharing the file.
A school radio segment that has to be family-friendly: bleep the one rude joke.

tool:RemoveAudio.summary: Removes all sound from a video and keeps the picture exactly as it was.
tool:RemoveAudio.details: Remove Audio makes a silent copy of a video. There is no window: it starts as soon as you drop. The picture is copied untouched, not re-encoded, so it is quick and loses no quality, and every audio track is left out. The copy is saved beside the original as 'name Muted', in the same format. You can drop many videos at once.
tool:RemoveAudio.how: Drag one or more videos, tap Ctrl and drop on MUTE; the silent copies appear next to the originals.
examples: A phone video full of wind noise that you want to put music under later.
A screen recording where your keyboard and a TV can be heard: share the silent copy instead.
Five clips for a slideshow that will get its own soundtrack: drop all five at once.
tool:RemoveAudio.worksOn: Videos (MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, AVI, WMV); one or many at once. Not GIFs.

tool:TrimVideo.summary: Cuts the start and end off a video or GIF, keeping just the part you choose.
tool:TrimVideo.details: Trim Video shows a filmstrip of the video with two handles: drag the ends to choose the part to keep, or type the Start and End times. The header shows how long the selection is, and the preview plays only the selected part (Space plays, the arrow keys step one frame). By default the cut is exact to the frame and the video is re-encoded; Fast trim (no re-encoding, cuts at keyframes) is instant and lossless but may start slightly earlier. Choose Apply to save 'name Trimmed' in the same format.
tool:TrimVideo.how: Drag one video, tap Ctrl and drop on TRIM; drag the ends of the filmstrip and choose Apply.
examples: A 3-minute phone video of a goal where only 20 seconds matter: drag both handles around the goal.
A Zoom recording that starts with 2 minutes of waiting: move the start handle and tick Fast trim to finish instantly.
A funny GIF that goes on too long: trim it to the best two seconds.

tool:CropVideo.summary: Cuts away the edges of a video's picture, freely or to a shape such as square or 9:16.
tool:CropVideo.details: Crop Video shows a frame of the video with a crop box you drag and resize. Aspect ratio is Free, 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3 or 3:4, and Size shows the box in pixels; type a width (W) and height (H) to set it exactly. A slider and the frame step buttons move through the video so you can check the box at other moments. Reset clears the box and the ratio. Choose Apply to save 'name Cropped' in the same format; the sound is kept.
tool:CropVideo.how: Drag one video, tap Ctrl and drop on CROP; drag the crop box, pick a ratio if you want, and choose Apply.
examples: A screen recording that shows the taskbar along the bottom: crop it off.
A landscape video for a square Instagram post: choose 1:1 and move the box onto the people.
A GIF with black bars at the top and bottom: crop them away.

tool:ChangeSpeed.summary: Speeds a video up or slows it down, from 0.25× to 4×, keeping voices at their natural pitch.
tool:ChangeSpeed.details: Change Video Speed has a Playback speed slider with six stops: 0.25×, 0.5×, 1×, 1.5×, 2× and 4×. Keep the voice's pitch is on by default, so fast speech doesn't sound like a chipmunk; turn it off for that effect. The preview plays at the chosen speed when Windows can play the file. Picture and sound change together, and silent videos and GIFs work too. Apply is available once you pick a speed other than 1×; the copy is saved as, for example, 'name Speed 2x' in the same format.
tool:ChangeSpeed.how: Drag one video, tap Ctrl and drop on SPEED; move the slider to a speed and choose Apply.
examples: A 20-minute recorded lecture you want to get through in 10: choose 2×.
A shot of a child blowing out birthday candles in slow motion: choose 0.5×.
A long screen recording of a software install turned into a quick timelapse: choose 4×.

tool:VideoSnapshots.summary: Saves chosen frames of a video as full-size PNG pictures.
tool:VideoSnapshots.details: Video Snapshots shows the video with a slider and frame step buttons; the arrow keys step one frame at a time. At each moment you want, choose Add Frame or press Enter; the frame appears as a tile with its time, and you can click a tile to go back to it or remove it with its X. The button counts the frames (for example Save 3 Frames) and saves them at the video's full resolution. They are saved beside the video as 'name Snapshot.png', 'name Snapshot 2.png' and so on.
tool:VideoSnapshots.how: Drag one video, tap Ctrl and drop on SNAPSHOT; move to a moment, choose Add Frame, then choose Save Frames.
examples: The perfect smile from a birthday video, saved as a photo to print.
Three slides from a recorded webinar, kept as pictures for your notes.
A YouTube thumbnail taken from the clip itself.

tool:SplitVideo.summary: Cuts one video into several clips at the moments you choose, or into equal parts.
tool:SplitVideo.details: Split Video shows a filmstrip of the video. Move to a moment and choose Add Split to put a split point there; the number of points is shown, and Reset clears them. Equal clips sets a number from 2 to 50 with the minus and plus buttons, and Set spreads the split points evenly. Choose Split Video: the clips go into a new folder 'name Clips' beside the video, as 'name 1', 'name 2' and so on, in the same format. Each cut is exact to the frame (the clips are re-encoded).
tool:SplitVideo.how: Drag one video, tap Ctrl and drop on SPLIT; add split points or set Equal clips and choose Set, then choose Split Video.
examples: A 10-minute video for WhatsApp Status in 30-second pieces: set Equal clips to 20.
A recorded class with three topics: add a split at the start of each new topic.
A wedding film divided into the ceremony and the party.

tool:RedactVideo.summary: Hides faces, number plates or text in a video with a solid box or a strong blur, for as long as you choose.
tool:RedactVideo.details: Redact Video lets you draw boxes on the video's picture. Style is Solid (in a colour you pick, black by default) or Blur, which is strong enough that faces and text can't be made out. Each box gets its own lane under Redactions: drag its ends to choose when the box is visible; at first it covers the whole video. The boxes stay where you draw them; they don't follow moving things. Reset removes all boxes, and Save Redacted Copy saves 'name Redacted' in the same format with the sound kept.
tool:RedactVideo.how: Drag one video, tap Ctrl and drop on REDACT; draw a box over what to hide, set its lane, and choose Save Redacted Copy.
examples: A dashcam clip to post online that shows another car's number plate: blur it.
A screen recording where your e-mail address shows for 10 seconds: a black box for just those seconds.
A school play video where one child's face must not be shown.

tool:JoinVideos.summary: Joins several videos into one MP4, in the order you set.
tool:JoinVideos.details: Join Videos opens a Playback order list of your videos; drag a row or use its up and down buttons to change the order. Choose Join Videos to make one MP4 (H.264 with AAC sound). The first video sets the frame size and frame rate; the others are fitted inside it with black bars where their shapes differ, and clips without sound get silence so the sound stays in step. The result is saved beside the first video in the list as 'name Joined.mp4'.
tool:JoinVideos.how: Select two or more videos, drag them, tap Ctrl and drop on JOIN; set the order and choose Join Videos.
examples: Six short phone clips from a holiday made into one video to send the family.
An intro, the main recording and an outro put together for a YouTube upload.
Two halves of a recording that stopped in the middle, joined back into one.
tool:JoinVideos.worksOn: Two or more videos at once.

tool:Transcribe.summary: Writes down what is said in a recording or video, as subtitles or text, using Whisper on this PC.
tool:Transcribe.details: Transcribe uses the Whisper speech model on your PC: Accuracy is Fast, Balanced or Accurate (one-time downloads of about 60 MB, 190 MB and 574 MB), and Accurate is best for Arabic, accents and noisy recordings. Language is Detect automatically or one of 22 languages, and Subtitles in is As spoken, In English or In Arabic: speech already in the language wanted is written as spoken; Arabic goes into English and English into Arabic through the Opus-MT translation models (one-time downloads of about 114 MB each), and other languages go into English with Whisper's own translation (Accurate can't translate, so Balanced or Fast does it) and from there into Arabic. Save as gives Subtitles (an .srt file), Text (a .txt file) or Both, named like the original (talk.srt) so video players load the subtitles by themselves. For a video, In the video can also put the subtitles into a copy, As a track (switched on and off in the player) or Burned in (part of the picture), saved as 'name Subtitled'. The graphics card speeds it up when it can, and you can do many files at once.
tool:Transcribe.how: Drag a recording or video, tap Ctrl and drop on SUBTITLES; choose the accuracy, language and what to save, then Transcribe. The first time, choose Download in the window to get the model.
examples: A 1-hour interview recorded on your phone turned into a text file to quote from: Save as › Text.
An Arabic family video with English subtitles for relatives abroad: Subtitles in › In English, In the video › Burned in.
A lecture video with subtitles students can switch on and off: In the video › As a track.
tool:Transcribe.worksOn: Audio and video files; one or many at once.

tool:RemoveNoise.summary: Takes hum, hiss, traffic and room noise out of speech in recordings and videos, on this PC.
tool:RemoveNoise.details: Remove Noise uses the DeepFilterNet 3 model on your PC, a one-time download of about 27 MB. Amount is Gentle (leaves a little of the room's sound, so the voice stays natural), Strong, or Full (the default, which takes out all the noise it can). It is made for speech: interviews, lectures, calls and videos. In a video only the sound changes; the picture is copied as it is. The result keeps the original format and is saved beside it as 'name Clean'.
tool:RemoveNoise.how: Drag recordings or videos, tap Ctrl and drop on DENOISE; pick an Amount and choose Remove Noise. From a command prompt: petal denoise <files> --strength gentle, strong or full.
examples: An interview recorded next to a noisy air conditioner: Full takes the hum away.
A lecture filmed on a phone with traffic outside the window: the voice comes through clearly.
A podcast recorded in a bare room where Full sounds too processed: try Gentle.
tool:RemoveNoise.worksOn: Audio and video files; one or many at once.

tool:SeparateVocals.summary: Splits a song into the voice and the music, or into vocals, drums, bass and other instruments.
tool:SeparateVocals.details: Separate Vocals uses the HT Demucs model on your PC, a one-time download of about 181 MB. Split into is Vocals and music (two files) or Four parts (vocals, drums, bass and the other instruments, each in its own file). The files go into a new folder 'name Stems' beside the original, named Vocals, Music, Drums, Bass and Other. Songs keep their format; the sound of a video is saved as M4A. A song of a few minutes takes a few minutes, and files up to 30 minutes long are accepted.
tool:SeparateVocals.how: Drag a song or video, tap Ctrl and drop on VOCALS; choose Vocals and music or Four parts, then Separate. From a command prompt: petal separate <files> (add --four for four parts).
examples: A karaoke version of a favourite song: keep Music.mp3 from the Stems folder.
A singer's voice on its own, to practise harmonies against it.
A drummer who wants a song without drums to play along: choose Four parts and mix the others.
tool:SeparateVocals.worksOn: Audio and video files; one or many at once.

tool:TranslateSubtitles.summary: Translates English subtitle files into Arabic on this PC, keeping every cue's timing.
tool:TranslateSubtitles.details: Translate to Arabic reads an English SRT or VTT subtitle file and translates it cue by cue with the Opus-MT model, a one-time download of about 114 MB. The timing stays unchanged, and formatting tags are left out of the translation. The result is saved beside the original with '.ar' in the name (talk.srt becomes talk.ar.srt), so players offer it as Arabic. It translates from English only; for a video in another language, use Transcribe with Subtitles in › In Arabic.
tool:TranslateSubtitles.how: Drag one or more .srt or .vtt files, tap Ctrl and drop on ARABIC, then choose Translate. From a command prompt: petal translate <subtitles>.
examples: English subtitles downloaded for a film, translated for a parent who reads Arabic.
A course's lecture captions in VTT, translated for Arabic-speaking students.
English subtitles you made earlier with Transcribe, turned into Arabic later.
tool:TranslateSubtitles.worksOn: Subtitle files (SRT and VTT); one or many at once.

tool:RemovePauses.summary: Cuts the silent stretches out of a talk, lesson or screen recording, picture and sound together.
tool:RemovePauses.details: Remove Pauses finds the quiet parts of a video or recording and cuts them out in one pass. A pause is sets how quiet counts (Very quiet, Quiet by default, or Noisy for recordings with background sound), At least sets the shortest pause removed (0.4 s, 0.6 s by default, 1 s or 2 s), and Kept at each cut leaves A little, Some (default) or More of each pause so words aren't clipped. For one file the window says how many pauses it found and how much shorter the result will be, and updates as you change the choices. Choose Remove Pauses; the result is saved as 'name No pauses' in the same format, and when no pauses that long are found nothing is written and the card says so. The file needs sound.
tool:RemovePauses.how: Drag a video or recording, tap Ctrl and drop on PAUSES; check the estimate, adjust the choices and choose Remove Pauses.
examples: A 25-minute screen-recorded tutorial full of thinking gaps comes out at about 18 minutes.
A voice-over for a presentation with long breaths between slides, tightened up in one go.
A recorded lecture with the noisy hall set to Noisy so the real pauses are found.
tool:RemovePauses.worksOn: Videos and audio files; one or many at once.

tool:AnimatedCaptions.summary: Burns moving captions into a video, a few words at a time with the spoken word lit up, like short videos.
tool:AnimatedCaptions.details: Animated Captions listens to the video with the Whisper speech model on your PC and draws the words into the picture. Style is Word by word (a short line with the word being said lit up and a little larger), One word (one big word at a time, popping in) or Lines (plain bold lines); Place is Bottom, Middle or Top; Size is Small, Medium or Large; Lit word is yellow, green, pink, violet or blue. A frame of the video shows how the captions will look. Accuracy (Fast, Balanced or Accurate: downloads of about 60, 190 and 574 MB), Spoken in, and Words in (As spoken, In English or In Arabic; a translation model of about 114 MB the first time) work as in Transcribe. Choose Add Captions; the result is saved as 'name Captioned' with the sound kept, and Arabic reads right to left.
tool:AnimatedCaptions.how: Drag one or more videos, tap Ctrl and drop on CAPTION; pick a style, place and colour, then choose Add Captions.
examples: A talking-head clip for TikTok where yellow words light up as you speak: Word by word, Bottom.
A Reel most people watch with the sound off: One word, Middle, Large.
An English product video with Arabic captions for customers in the Gulf: Words in › In Arabic.
tool:AnimatedCaptions.worksOn: Videos; one or many at once.

tool:Reframe.summary: Makes a wide video tall (9:16) for Reels, Shorts and TikTok, following the person or showing the whole picture.
tool:Reframe.details: Vertical Video turns a landscape video into a 9:16 one. Tall window is Follow (the frame follows what moves; with the background model, a one-time download of about 224 MB, it follows people more surely and glides rather than jumps), Middle (the centre of the picture, top to bottom) or Whole picture (all of it, over a blurred, enlarged copy of itself). Size is 1080 × 1920 or 720 × 1280. A frame of the video shows where the tall window sits. Choose Make Vertical; the result is saved as 'name Vertical' in the same format with the sound kept.
tool:Reframe.how: Drag one or more videos, tap Ctrl and drop on VERTICAL; choose the Tall window and Size, then choose Make Vertical.
examples: A YouTube interview clip of one speaker made into a Short: Follow keeps them in frame as they move.
A landscape travel video for Instagram Reels where nothing should be cut off: Whole picture.
A webinar recording with the speaker standing in the centre: Middle at 720 × 1280 for a smaller file.
tool:Reframe.worksOn: Videos; one or many at once.

tool:MakeShorts.summary: Turns a long video (a talk, an interview, a podcast, a lesson) into short clips ready for Reels, Shorts and TikTok: its best moments, found, framed and captioned.
tool:MakeShorts.details: Make Shorts listens to the whole video on this PC (Whisper, with each word's time) and finds the moments that stand on their own: each starts where a sentence starts and ends where a thought ends. They are ranked by what keeps people watching: an opening that pulls you in (a question, “imagine…”), lively delivery, a story, advice, numbers, feeling or laughter, one topic from start to end, and the length asked for. Choose how many Clips (3, 5 or 8), their Length (up to 30 s, 30–60 s or 60–90 s), the Shape (Tall 9:16, Square or As filmed) and the Framing. Follow the speaker finds faces with Windows' own face detector, keeps the one talking in frame, glides as they move and cuts when someone else speaks; where no face is clear (slides, a stage) it shows the whole picture over a blurred copy instead, as Whole picture always does. Captions are burned in Word by word (the word being said lit up in the colour chosen), One word or Lines, and Words in is the language spoken, English or Arabic. Headline at the start puts a title over the first seconds; Cut the pauses tightens the silences between sentences. Choose Find the Best Moments: the moments appear best first, each with a score out of 100 and why it was chosen. Play one to check it, change its title (titles are written by the AI model on this PC when it is there, and kept only when they hold to what is said), untick any you don't want, then choose Make Shorts. The clips are saved in a new folder named 'name Shorts', numbered and titled, as MP4 at 1080 × 1920 with the sound at the loudness the apps play at. A video heard once opens again at once.
tool:MakeShorts.how: Drag a video, tap Ctrl and drop it on SHORTS; choose the number, length, shape and captions of the clips, choose Find the Best Moments, check the moments, then choose Make Shorts.
examples: A one-hour podcast into eight 60-second clips for TikTok, each opening with a question and captioned word by word.
An Arabic lecture into five Reels with Arabic captions and a headline, the pauses cut.
A recorded webinar with slides: Whole picture keeps the slides readable, with English captions under them.
tool:MakeShorts.worksOn: One video with speech, of any length.

tool:Dub.summary: Says a video's speech again in the other language, Arabic into English or English into Arabic, in each speaker's own voice; the music is taken out and every other sound is kept.
tool:Dub.details: Dub separates the voices from the rest of the sound (Demucs), writes down what is said with each word's time (Whisper) and translates it line by line, all on this PC. Choose the language to Dub into (Into English or Into Arabic), the language Spoken in (or Detect automatically) and the Accuracy of the listening, then choose Prepare the Dub. The lines appear with their translations: check them, change any that need it, and play a line to hear how it was said. Then choose Dub. First the music is taken out of the rest of the sound (by TIGER, made to split film sound into speech, music and effects), so steps, rain, wind and the hum of a room stay while the music goes; this takes a while the first time and is kept. Each line is then said again by the voice model on this PC (Chatterbox) in the voice of the person who said it, learnt from that very line; it is heard back and said again when it came out wrong, fitted into the time the original took (said up to 1.3 times quicker when it runs longer) and laid over the other sounds as loud as the original was said. The new video is saved next to the original as 'name Arabic.mp4' or 'name English.mp4', its picture untouched. Keep the original sound as a second track adds the original sound, music and all, for players that can switch tracks, and Subtitles in the new language puts the translation in the file as subtitles. The file says its voices were made by AI. A video prepared once opens again at once. Dub only videos whose speakers would agree to their voices being used.
tool:Dub.how: Drag a video, tap Ctrl and drop it on DUB; choose the language to dub into, choose Prepare the Dub, check the translations, then choose Dub.
examples: An English lesson dubbed into Arabic in the teacher's own voice, the background music taken out and the sounds of the class kept.
An Arabic interview dubbed into English, with English subtitles added.
A product video in English made Arabic without its music, two translations corrected before dubbing.
tool:Dub.worksOn: One video with speech in Arabic or English, up to 30 minutes long.

tool:Compress.summary: Makes pictures, videos, audio and PDFs smaller, by a preset, a target size, a percentage or an app's limit.
tool:Compress.details: Compress opens a window showing the original size, with four ways to shrink: Preset (Balanced, or Strong for much smaller files), For an app (WhatsApp, Email, Discord, Upload form or Instagram; WhatsApp is chosen first), Target size in MB per file, or Percentage (10 to 90% smaller, 50% at first). Videos can also be limited to 4K, 1080p, 720p or 480p, and pictures to 3840, 2560, 1920 or 1280 px on the longest side. PDFs have their pictures redrawn at the size they are shown and saved as JPEG (150 DPI in Balanced, 100 DPI in Strong); if a PDF can't get any smaller, the original stays the best version. WAV and AIFF audio become FLAC, which is lossless and about half the size. Each result is saved next to the original as 'name Compressed', and the card says how much was saved, such as '48 MB → 14 MB (71% smaller)'.
tool:Compress.how: Drag the files, tap Ctrl and drop on COMPRESS; choose a way to shrink and press Compress.
examples: A 48 MB phone video for WhatsApp: choose For an app › WhatsApp and it is made to fit under 16 MB.
A scanned 12 MB PDF for a university form: For an app › Upload form keeps it under 2 MB.
Thirty holiday photos for an e-mail: drop them together and pick For an app › Email so they fit in one 25 MB message.
tool:Compress.worksOn: Pictures, videos, GIFs, audio and PDFs; one file, many at once, or a dropped folder.

tool:CreatePdf.summary: Turns several pictures into one PDF, one page per picture, in the order they were selected.
tool:CreatePdf.details: Create PDF works straight away with no window: each picture becomes a page the size of the picture, in selection order. JPEG photos are placed in the PDF unchanged, so they keep their quality; WEBP, HEIC and AVIF pictures are stored inside as JPEG at quality 90, and SVG drawings are drawn at 300 dpi so they print sharply. Transparent areas become white. The PDF is named after the first picture (trip 1.jpg gives trip 1.pdf) and saved next to it. To make the text of scanned pages searchable as well, use Make Searchable (OCR) instead.
tool:CreatePdf.how: Select two or more pictures, drag them, tap Ctrl and drop on CREATE PDF.
examples: Five phone photos of a signed contract become one PDF to e-mail back.
Twelve scanned receipts in JPG go into a single PDF for an expense report.
Screenshots of a long chat put together as one PDF to keep or print.
tool:CreatePdf.worksOn: Two or more pictures, including Photoshop files and drawings such as SVG.

tool:SplitPdf.summary: Splits a PDF into separate one-page PDFs, saved together in a new folder.
tool:SplitPdf.details: Split PDF needs no settings: every page is saved as its own PDF named after the original and its page number (report 1.pdf, report 2.pdf and so on). The pages go into a new folder next to the PDF called 'report Pages'. Several PDFs dropped at once are each split into their own folder. The original PDF is not changed; to keep only some pages or change their order, use Organize PDF instead.
tool:SplitPdf.how: Drag the PDF, tap Ctrl and drop on SPLIT.
examples: A 20-page scanned bundle where each page is a different invoice: split it and send each page on its own.
A class handout PDF: split it to share only page 3 with a classmate.
Ten monthly bank statements at once: drop them together and each gets its own folder of pages.
tool:SplitPdf.worksOn: PDFs; one or many at once, or a dropped folder of PDFs.

tool:OrganizePdf.summary: Reorders, rotates, duplicates or removes the pages of a PDF and saves a new copy.
tool:OrganizePdf.details: Organize PDF opens a window with a thumbnail of every page and the page count. Drag pages to put them in a new order; rest the pointer on a page to rotate it, duplicate it or remove it. Reset Order puts the pages back as they were, and 'Make all pages the same width' scales pages to match the narrowest one (their heights may still differ). Save Organized PDF writes 'name Organized.pdf' next to the original, which is left as it is.
tool:OrganizePdf.how: Drag one PDF, tap Ctrl and drop on ORGANIZE; arrange the pages and press Save Organized PDF.
examples: A scan where pages 2 and 3 came out upside down: rotate them and save.
A 30-page report with two blank pages: remove them before sending.
A form whose signature page should come first: drag it to the front.

tool:MergePdfs.summary: Joins several PDFs into one, in the order you choose.
tool:MergePdfs.details: Merge PDFs opens a list titled Document order with every PDF you dropped. Drag a row, or use its up and down arrows, to change the order, then press Merge PDFs. The pages are joined into one file named after the first PDF in the list, such as 'chapter 1 Merged.pdf', saved next to it. Bookmarks inside the PDFs are kept and point at the right pages in the new file.
tool:MergePdfs.how: Select two or more PDFs, drag them, tap Ctrl and drop on MERGE PDF; set the order and press Merge PDFs.
examples: A CV, a cover letter and two certificates joined into one PDF for a job application.
Twelve monthly statements put together as one file for the tax adviser.
Chapters of a thesis saved as separate PDFs combined in the right order.

tool:ExtractArchive.summary: Unpacks ZIP, RAR, 7Z, TAR and TAR.GZ archives into a folder next to them.
tool:ExtractArchive.details: Extract Archive runs straight away with no window. When everything in the archive sits in one top-level folder, that folder is unpacked directly, so you don't get a folder inside a folder of the same name; otherwise a new folder named after the archive is made. Files keep their modified dates, and characters Windows doesn't allow in names are removed. Nothing is ever written outside the new folder, and several archives dropped together are each extracted on their own.
tool:ExtractArchive.how: Drag the archive, tap Ctrl and drop on EXTRACT.
examples: A ZIP of photos from a friend opens into a 'Holiday' folder next to it.
A RAR file of course materials extracted without installing WinRAR.
A folder full of 7Z backups: drop the folder, tap Ctrl and choose EXTRACT to unpack every archive inside.
tool:ExtractArchive.worksOn: ZIP, RAR, 7Z, TAR and TAR.GZ (TGZ, GZ) archives; one or many, or archives inside a dropped folder.

tool:ProtectPdf.summary: Locks a PDF with a password (AES-256), or saves a copy without the password you know.
tool:ProtectPdf.details: The Password window checks the PDF first. For a PDF without a password, type it under Password and Confirm, choose whether to allow printing and copying text and pictures (both on) and changes and comments (off), then press Protect; the copy 'name Protected.pdf' is encrypted with AES-256, can't be opened without the password, and the password can't be recovered. For a PDF that already has a password, type it and press Remove Password to save 'name Unlocked.pdf', which opens freely; the original keeps its password. With several PDFs, all are handled the way the first one is, and the others are skipped with a note. A password with Arabic letters must start and end with one and can't also contain Latin letters.
tool:ProtectPdf.how: Drag the PDF, tap Ctrl and drop on PASSWORD; type the password and press Protect or Remove Password.
examples: A payslip PDF to e-mail: protect it with a password you tell the person by phone.
A bank statement that asks for a password every time: remove it once and keep a copy that opens directly.
Five contracts at once: drop them together and they all get the same password.
tool:ProtectPdf.worksOn: PDFs; one or many at once.

tool:NumberPages.summary: Adds page numbers as real text to every page of a PDF, with a live preview.
tool:NumberPages.details: Add Page Numbers shows a preview of a page with the number where it will go. Choose Position (Bottom or Top), Align (Left, Centre or Right), Style (1, 1 / 12 or - 1 -), Size (7 to 24 pt, 10 at first) and Start at (1 at first). 'Leave the first page unnumbered (a cover)' starts the numbers on page two. Press Add Numbers to save 'name Numbered.pdf'; a PDF with a password, or locked against changes by its author, has to be unlocked first.
tool:NumberPages.how: Drag the PDF, tap Ctrl and drop on NUMBERS; choose where the numbers go and press Add Numbers.
examples: A 40-page thesis printed for binding gets numbers at the bottom centre, with the cover left unnumbered.
Meeting papers numbered '1 / 12' so everyone can find the same page.
A second volume that should start at page 101: set Start at to 101.
tool:NumberPages.worksOn: PDFs; one or many at once, or a dropped folder of PDFs.

tool:SignPdf.summary: Places your drawn, typed or scanned signature on a PDF page as a picture.
tool:SignPdf.details: Sign PDF shows the page with your signature on it as you work. Under Signature choose Draw (sign with the mouse or a pen; Clear starts again), Type (your name in a handwriting-style font) or Picture (choose a PNG, JPG or other picture of your signature). Then choose Pages (Last page at first, First page or Every page), Position (one of nine spots, bottom right at first) and Size (10 to 60%, 28% at first), and press Sign to save 'name Signed.pdf'. The signature is a picture on the page, not a certificate-based digital signature.
tool:SignPdf.how: Drag one PDF, tap Ctrl and drop on SIGN; draw, type or choose your signature and press Sign.
examples: A rental agreement e-mailed as a PDF: draw your signature on the last page and send it back.
A permission slip from school: type your name and it is placed in a handwriting style.
A photo of your signature on paper placed on every page of a contract with Every page.

tool:ExtractImages.summary: Saves every picture inside a PDF into a new folder, each picture once.
tool:ExtractImages.details: Extract Images works straight away with no window. JPEG pictures are saved exactly as they are stored in the PDF, without compressing them again; other pictures are saved as PNG. A picture that appears many times, such as a logo on every page, is saved only once. The pictures go into a folder next to the PDF named 'name Images'.
tool:ExtractImages.how: Drag the PDF, tap Ctrl and drop on IMAGES.
examples: A product catalogue PDF: pull out all the product photos for a website.
A wedding album sent as a PDF: get the photos back at their full quality.
A report with charts: save the charts as pictures to put in slides.
tool:ExtractImages.worksOn: PDFs; one or many at once, or a dropped folder of PDFs.

tool:MakeSearchable.summary: Reads scanned PDFs and photos of pages with Windows OCR so their text can be searched and copied.
tool:MakeSearchable.details: Make Searchable works straight away: every page that has no text of its own is read with Windows' built-in OCR (every installed language is tried, Arabic included) and gets an invisible text layer exactly over the words. The page looks the same, but search, selection and copy now work. Each PDF is saved as 'name Searchable.pdf', and several pictures dropped together become the pages of one searchable PDF named after the first picture. A PDF whose pages all have text already is left alone, and when no text is found the card suggests a sharper scan or adding its language under Windows Settings › Time & language.
tool:MakeSearchable.how: Drag the scanned PDF (or several photos of pages), tap Ctrl and drop on OCR.
examples: A scanned 30-page contract: make it searchable, then find every mention of 'termination' with Ctrl+F.
Five phone photos of book pages become one PDF you can copy quotes from.
An Arabic letter scanned as a PDF: its text can then be copied into Word.
tool:MakeSearchable.worksOn: PDFs (one or many, or a dropped folder of PDFs), or two or more pictures.

tool:ReadAloud.summary: Turns a PDF, Word file, e-book or text into an MP3 audiobook spoken on this PC.
tool:ReadAloud.details: Read Aloud reads the document's text and shows how many words it has and about how many minutes it will take. It picks a voice for the document's language: one of Windows' own voices, or the natural voices Kareem (Arabic) and Joe (English), which download once from the window (about 85 MB each). Choose Speed (0.75×, 1×, 1.25× or 1.5×), press Listen to hear the first sentences, then Save Audio to write 'name Audio.mp3' next to the document. If no installed voice speaks the document's language, Open Speech Settings lets Windows add one; the text never leaves the PC.
tool:ReadAloud.how: Drag the document, tap Ctrl and drop on LISTEN; choose a voice and speed and press Save Audio.
examples: A 25-page PDF chapter to listen to on the bus: save it as an MP3 at 1.25×.
An Arabic article in Word read by the natural Kareem voice.
An EPUB novel turned into an audiobook for a long drive.
tool:ReadAloud.worksOn: One file: PDF, Word (DOCX), ODT, RTF, Markdown, HTML, TXT or EPUB.

tool:FileDetails.summary: Shows what a design file holds: size, colour, layers, pages, fonts and linked files, found or missing.
tool:FileDetails.details: File Info opens a window that reads the file without any Adobe application. For Photoshop files it shows the size in pixels, the resolution, the colour mode and bit depth, the layers (text layers, smart objects, groups, hidden layers), whether a flat copy is saved, the Photoshop history, the fonts and the placed files. For camera RAW photos it shows the camera, lens, exposure (shutter, aperture, ISO, focal length) and size; for Illustrator, EPS, InDesign (INDD, IDML) and XD files it shows the main facts, the fonts (installed on this PC or not) and the linked files (found or missing). A preview is shown when one can be drawn, and for files that can be gathered a Collect Files… button opens Collect Files.
tool:FileDetails.how: Drag the file, tap Ctrl and drop on INFO; press Done when you have read it.
examples: A PSD from a designer: check which fonts it uses and which aren't installed before opening it.
An InDesign file that prints with missing pictures: see which linked files are missing.
A RAW photo from a camera: check the lens, shutter speed and ISO it was taken with.
tool:FileDetails.worksOn: One Photoshop (PSD, PSB), camera RAW, Illustrator (AI), EPS, InDesign (INDD, IDML) or XD file.

tool:CollectFiles.summary: Gathers a design or video project with every file and font it uses into one folder, with a report.
tool:CollectFiles.details: Collect Files lists every file the project uses, found or missing, with the total size and the fonts it needs. Press Collect to copy the project and its pictures and footage into a new folder 'name Collected', with pictures under Links (Media for video projects) and, when 'Copy the fonts too' is on, the installed fonts under Document fonts. A report, 'Collected files.txt', lists what was copied and what was missing. Premiere Pro, After Effects and IDML copies are pointed at the collected files so they open anywhere; InDesign and Illustrator copies still point at the original places and may need relinking to the Links folder.
tool:CollectFiles.how: Drag the project file, tap Ctrl and drop on COLLECT; check the list and press Collect.
examples: An InDesign brochure sent to the print shop with all its photos and fonts.
A Premiere Pro project moved to a new laptop with every clip it uses.
An Illustrator logo file archived together with the pictures it links to.
tool:CollectFiles.worksOn: One Premiere Pro (PRPROJ), After Effects (AEP), InDesign (INDD, INDT, IDML) or Illustrator (AI) file.

tool:OrganizeFolder.summary: Sorts the files of a folder into folders by kind or by month, with screenshots and invoices apart.
tool:OrganizeFolder.details: Organize Folder moves files within the dropped folder; nothing is copied or deleted, and History can put everything back. Sort By kind makes folders such as Pictures, Videos, Music, Documents, Archives and Installers, with 'Screenshots in a folder of their own' and 'Invoices and receipts in a folder of their own' (both on; invoices are found by reading the text of PDFs and photos), and other files stay where they are. By month puts files into year and month folders (2024 › 2024-07): photos by the day they were taken, the rest by the day they last changed. You can also rename photos after the moment they were taken (2024-07-15 18.30.05) and include files in subfolders (both off at first); a summary shows how many files go where before you press Organize.
tool:OrganizeFolder.how: Drag the folder, tap Ctrl and drop on ORGANIZE; choose By kind or By month and press Organize.
examples: A messy Downloads folder of 600 files sorted into Pictures, Documents, Installers and Invoices.
A phone backup of 3,000 photos put into folders by year and month.
A desktop full of screenshots moved into a Screenshots folder of its own.

tool:FolderPdf.summary: Puts every picture and PDF in a folder, in folder order, into one PDF next to the folder.
tool:FolderPdf.details: Folder to PDF shows how many pictures and PDFs will be used, in the order they have in the folder; each PDF's pages follow in their place. Under Pages choose Picture size (each page the size of its picture), A4 or Letter. 'Include subfolders' is on at first, and 'Read the text of scanned pages, so the PDF can be searched' adds OCR (off at first). Press Create PDF to save one PDF named after the folder beside it, so a folder called Trip gives Trip.pdf.
tool:FolderPdf.how: Drag the folder, tap Ctrl and drop on ONE PDF; choose the page size and press Create PDF.
examples: A folder of 40 scanned pages from a phone app becomes one searchable PDF.
A 'Visa application' folder with passport photos and PDF forms joined into one file to upload.
A folder of course handouts in PDF turned into one file to print in one go.
tool:FolderPdf.worksOn: A dropped folder with pictures or PDFs (several folders each get their own PDF).

tool:ContactSheet.summary: Makes a PDF of small prints of every picture in a folder, with their names, page after page.
tool:ContactSheet.details: Contact Sheet lays the pictures of a folder out in a grid on paper. Choose Columns (3, 4, 5 or 6; 4 at first) and Paper (A4, A4 landscape or Letter), and keep or turn off 'Show file names' and 'Include subfolders' (both on at first). The summary shows how many pictures and pages there will be and how many pictures go on a page. Press Create Contact Sheet to save 'Trip Contact Sheet.pdf' beside the folder, with the folder's name printed on every page and the pages numbered.
tool:ContactSheet.how: Drag a folder of pictures, tap Ctrl and drop on CONTACT SHEET; choose the columns and paper and press Create Contact Sheet.
examples: A photographer sends a client one PDF of 200 shots to choose from by file name.
A class's photos printed on two A4 pages to check who is in which picture.
A folder of product photos reviewed at a glance before a catalogue is made.

tool:FolderReport.summary: Makes an Excel or CSV list of every file in a folder, and shows what takes the space.
tool:FolderReport.details: Folder Report lists every file with its name, folder, type, size, and modified and created dates. With 'Picture sizes, durations and page counts' on (on at first for up to 1,000 files) it also reads each file for width, height, duration and pages, which takes longer. In Excel the workbook adds sheets for the space taken by each kind of file, the largest folders and the largest files; CSV holds the file list only. 'Include subfolders' is on at first, and Create Report saves 'Trip Report.xlsx' (or .csv) beside the folder.
tool:FolderReport.how: Drag the folder, tap Ctrl and drop on REPORT; choose Excel or CSV and press Create Report.
examples: A full external drive: find which folders and files take the most space.
A list of every video in a project folder with its duration, for an invoice.
An inventory of a shared office folder sent to IT as a spreadsheet.
tool:FolderReport.worksOn: A dropped folder (several folders each get their own report).

tool:GatherFiles.summary: Copies every file out of a folder's subfolders into one flat folder, or only pictures, videos, music or PDFs.
tool:GatherFiles.details: Gather Files looks through the folder and all its subfolders. Under Files choose All files, or only Pictures, Videos, Music or PDFs (only kinds that are in the folder are offered), and the summary says how many files will be copied. Press Gather Files to copy them into one new folder beside it, such as 'Trip (Gathered)'; files with the same name are numbered and the originals stay where they are.
tool:GatherFiles.how: Drag the folder, tap Ctrl and drop on GATHER; choose which files and press Gather Files.
examples: A camera card with photos spread over 30 date folders, gathered into one folder.
All the PDFs scattered through a 'University' folder tree copied into one place.
Every song from artist and album folders put in one folder for a car's USB stick.
tool:GatherFiles.worksOn: A dropped folder with subfolders (or several folders).

tool:CompareFiles.summary: Compares two versions of a document, or two pictures, and shows what changed on a page in your browser.
tool:CompareFiles.details: Compare Files needs exactly two files and runs straight away. For documents (Word, PDF, text, Markdown, HTML or e-books, even a PDF against its Word original) the words added and removed are marked in place, with long unchanged parts folded away; for PDFs the pages are also drawn side by side with what looks different boxed (the first 40 pages are drawn; the text is compared in full). For two pictures the places that differ are boxed, red on the old one and green on the new one. The older file (by when it last changed) counts as Before, and the report 'old vs new.html' is saved beside the newer file (or in the folder Settings › Results names) and opens in your browser.
tool:CompareFiles.how: Select the two files, drag them, tap Ctrl and drop on COMPARE.
examples: A contract the other side sent back: compare it with your version to see every changed word.
A PDF quote checked against the Word file it was made from.
Two versions of a poster compared to spot what the designer moved.
tool:CompareFiles.worksOn: Exactly two files: two documents (PDF, DOCX, ODT, RTF, MD, HTML, TXT, EPUB) or two pictures.

action:Ask.summary: Does what you ask with the files, in your own words in English or Arabic, after showing you the steps.
action:Ask.details: Ask DropWheel opens a box where you type (or say, with the microphone button) what to do, such as 'make them 1080 px WEBP and zip them' or 'put them in one searchable PDF'. DropWheel lists the steps it understood under 'DropWheel will:' and warns when they don't fit the files; nothing runs until you press Run. Common requests are understood without a model, and with the AI model (Qwen2.5 1.5B, about 1.1 GB, downloaded once from the window) requests worded freely are understood too, all on this PC. Save as Recipe… keeps the steps as a petal on the tools wheel, and results are saved beside the originals as 'name' plus the recipe's name.
action:Ask.how: Drag the files, tap Alt and drop on ASK; type what you want, press Ask, check the steps and press Run.
examples: Twenty phone photos: type 'compress them for WhatsApp' and send them right after.
Scans of an ID card: say 'put them in one searchable PDF'.
A batch of product photos: 'make them 1080 px WEBP and zip them', then Save as Recipe… for next time.

action:Share.summary: Opens the Windows share window to send files with Nearby Sharing, Mail, Teams or another app.
action:Share.details: Share hands the dropped files and folders to Windows' own share window, the same one apps use. From there you can send them with Nearby Sharing to a PC close by, or to any app that offers sharing, such as Mail or Teams. DropWheel doesn't upload anything itself; what happens next is up to the app you pick.
action:Share.how: Drag the files, tap Alt and drop on SHARE, then pick where to send them in the Windows share window.
examples: A presentation sent to a colleague's laptop in the same room with Nearby Sharing.
Three photos attached to a new e-mail in the Mail app.
A PDF passed straight into a Teams chat.
action:Share.worksOn: Files and folders; one or many.

action:Phone.summary: Shows a QR code so a phone on the same Wi-Fi can save the files, with nothing going through the internet.
action:Phone.details: Send to Phone starts a small sharing page on this PC and shows its QR code and address. Scan it with the phone's camera: the page lists the files to tap and save, folders download as ZIP, and 'Download everything as ZIP' takes it all. Turn on 'Let the phone send files to this PC' and the phone can send files back, saved in Downloads. When photos or videos record where they were taken, Share Without Location offers clean copies instead; sharing stops when you press Stop Sharing, close the window, or after 15 minutes with nothing happening. If Windows asks, allow DropWheel on private networks; on a network set to Public the phone can't reach the PC.
action:Phone.how: Drag the files, tap Alt and drop on TO PHONE, then scan the QR code with the phone's camera.
examples: Holiday videos moved from the PC to an iPhone without a cable or a cloud upload.
A PDF ticket put on an Android phone before leaving for the airport.
Photos from the phone sent to the PC's Downloads folder with 'Let the phone send files to this PC'.
action:Phone.worksOn: Files and folders; one or many.

action:SendToPc.summary: Sends files and folders straight to another PC with DropWheel on the same network, which asks before saving.
action:SendToPc.details: Send to PC looks for PCs on your network where DropWheel is receiving and lists them by name; Look Again searches once more. Choose one and that PC shows who wants to send how many files and how big they are, with Accept and Decline (it declines by itself after two minutes). Accepted files are saved in Downloads\DropWheel on that PC, and a card here says when they were sent, refused, or couldn't get through. The other PC must turn on 'Let other PCs send me files' in Settings › Work & Sharing, since receiving is off until then; nothing goes through the internet.
action:SendToPc.how: Drag the files, tap Alt, open MORE and drop on TO PC; then choose the PC to send to.
examples: A 3 GB video sent from a desktop to the laptop in the next room.
Scanned documents passed from the office PC to a colleague's PC.
A folder of photos moved to the family PC without a USB stick.
action:SendToPc.worksOn: Files and folders; one or many.

action:Clean.summary: Makes copies of photos, videos, PDFs and Office files without location, device and author details.
action:Clean.details: Clean for Sharing runs straight away with no window. Each copy is saved beside the original as 'name Clean' (photo Clean.jpg), without where a photo or video was taken, which device made it, or who wrote a PDF or Office file; pictures keep their colour profile and orientation, and sound and video are copied without being re-encoded. Audio and Photoshop files can be cleaned too. A dropped folder gets a cleaned copy beside it, such as 'Trip (Clean)', and files that can't be cleaned are left out.
action:Clean.how: Drag the files or folder, tap Alt and drop on CLEAN.
examples: House photos for a sale ad: clean them so the GPS location isn't in the pictures.
A Word CV sent to employers without your old company's name as its author.
A folder of event photos cleaned before posting them online.
action:Clean.worksOn: Photos, videos, audio, PDFs, Office files and Photoshop files; one or many, or folders.

action:Float.summary: Keeps files on a small floating shelf above every window, ready to drag into another app.
action:Float.details: Float opens a shelf that stays above other windows and shows the files as tiles. Drag a tile out into any app or folder, and drop more files onto the shelf to add them; dropping on FLOAT again adds to the same shelf. The pin button tucks the shelf into the screen edge, the bin button clears it, and the X closes it. A file that is moved away leaves the shelf.
action:Float.how: Drag the files, tap Alt and drop on FLOAT; later drag them from the shelf into the app you need.
examples: Five photos parked on the shelf while you open the web form you will upload them to.
Files picked from three different folders, then dropped into one e-mail together.
A logo kept at the screen edge to drag into several slides.
action:Float.worksOn: Files and folders; one or many.

action:Copy.summary: Copies files to the clipboard, ready to paste in File Explorer with Ctrl+V.
action:Copy.details: Copy puts the dropped files and folders on the clipboard, as File Explorer does with Ctrl+C. Paste them with Ctrl+V in any folder, or in an app that accepts pasted files. Pasting makes copies; the originals stay where they are.
action:Copy.how: Drag the files, tap Alt and drop on COPY, then press Ctrl+V where you want them.
examples: Photos copied while dragging, then pasted into a USB drive's folder.
A report copied and pasted into a chat app that accepts files.
Files from search results copied in one go to paste into a project folder.
action:Copy.worksOn: Files and folders; one or many.

action:Move.summary: Moves the original files to a folder you choose.
action:Move.details: Move opens a folder picker that starts in the files' own folder. Pick the destination and the originals are moved there with Windows' own copy engine, so its progress window and its questions about names already there appear as usual. A card then says how many items moved; click it to see them in File Explorer. DropWheel's History keeps the move, so you can put the files back from there.
action:Move.how: Drag the files, tap Alt and drop on MOVE, then choose the folder.
examples: Finished invoices moved from Downloads into the Accounts folder.
Phone photos moved off the desktop onto an external drive.
Old project files moved into an Archive folder to tidy up.
action:Move.worksOn: Files and folders; one or many.

action:Rename.summary: Renames many files at once with a pattern, numbers, dates or what's inside, previewed first.
action:Rename.details: Rename opens with the pattern {name} and buttons that add Name, Number, Date, Folder and What's inside to it. Number counts up from Start at, Date is when the photo was taken (or the file last changed) written as 2024-07-15, and What's inside reads each file on this PC for a document's title, an invoice's sender, a screenshot's words or what a photo shows. Find and Replace with change part of the names, and Letters sets As is, lower, UPPER or Title Case. A live list shows old and new names and flags a name that would be empty, the same name twice, or a name that already exists; after Rename, click the card to undo, and History keeps it too.
action:Rename.how: Drag the files, tap Alt and drop on RENAME; build the new name and press Rename.
